δουλιχίου: Δουλίχιον — Dulichium, an island kingdom near Ithaca; neut. gen. sg.

θαρσύνων: θαρσύνω — encourage, hearten; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’heartening’

θεόθεν: θεόθεν — from the gods, by the gods’ will; adv., -θεν suffix of source
θρόνοισιν: θρόνος — chair, seat; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
κακομήχανε: κακομήχανος — contriving evil, of evil devices; masc. voc. sg.
καταβλώσκοντα: καταβλώσκω — go down; pres. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’going down’
κατακτείνειν: κατακτείνω — kill, slay (= Attic ἀποκτείνω); pres. inf.
κατιοῦσαν: κάτειμι — go down, come down (to a harbour); pres. part. fem. acc. sg.: ’coming in’

κτενέω: κτείνω — kill, slay; fut. 1 sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic κτενῶ): ’I will kill’
λαερτιάδην: Λαερτιάδης — son of Laertes, patronymic of Odysseus; masc. acc. sg.
ληϊστῆρσιν: ληϊστήρ — raider, pirate (Attic ληστής); masc. dat. pl., epic -σιν
λιμέν: λιμήν — harbour; masc. acc. sg., elided (λιμέν’ = λιμένα)
λόφος: λόφος — ridge, hill; masc. nom. sg.
μάργε: μάργος — mad, frenzied, reckless; masc. voc. sg., in address
μάρτυρος: μάρτυρος — witness (o-stem by-form of Attic μάρτυς); masc. nom. sg., predicative
μέγαρόνδε: μέγαρον — hall, house; μέγαρόνδε ’to the hall’, adv., -δε suffix of direction
μνάᾳ: μνάομαι — woo, court (as a suitor); pres. 2 sg. mid., contracted (-άῃ → -ᾳ): ’you court’
μνήσαντο: μιμνήσκω — remind; mid. remember, think of (+ gen.); aor. 3 pl. mid., unaugmented (= ἐμνήσαντο)
μνηστήρεσσι: μνηστήρ — suitor; masc. dat. pl., epic -εσσι
νίσου: Νῖσος — Nisus, father of Amphinomus; masc. gen. sg.
οἶσθ: οἶδα — know; perf. 2 sg. with pres. sense, elided (οἶσθ’ = οἶσθα): ’you know’
παύσαντο: παύω — stop; mid. cease (+ gen.); aor. 3 pl. mid., unaugmented (= ἐπαύσαντο)

ποιήεντος: ποιήεις — grassy, rich in grass; masc./neut. gen. sg., epic -ήεντος
πολλάκι: πολλάκι(ς) — many times, often; adv., epic (= Attic πολλάκις)
πολυπύρου: πολύπυρος — rich in wheat; masc./neut. gen. sg.
σάκεσσι: σάκος — shield; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι
ταφίοισιν: Τάφιος — Taphian, of Taphos, a seafaring people; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν (= Attic -οις)
τρομέεσθαι: τρομέω (mid. τρομέομαι) — tremble, fear; pres. inf. mid., epic uncontracted -έεσθαι (= Attic -εῖσθαι): ’to dread’
υἱέϊ: υἱός — son; masc. dat. sg., epic υἱέϊ (= Attic υἱῷ)
φίλτατός: φίλος — dear; superl. φίλτατος, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’dearest’
φαγέειν: ἐσθίω (aor. ἔφαγον) — eat, devour; aor. inf., epic uncontracted (= Attic φαγεῖν)
φανῆναι: φαίνω — show; pass. appear; aor. pass. inf.: ’to appear’
ἀκαχίζεις: ἀκαχίζω — distress, grieve; pres. 2 sg., epic reduplicated present: ’you grieve’

ἀπαγγέλλων: ἀπαγγέλλω — report, bring word; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’bringing word’

ἐνιαύσιον: ἐνιαύσιος — a year old, yearly; masc. acc. sg.: ’yearling’
ἐπέσχε: ἐπέχω — hold out, hold to, offer; aor. 3 sg.: ’held out’

ἐρωήσει: ἐρωέω — rush, gush; fut. 3 sg.: ’will gush’

ἔδεις: ἔδω — eat, devour; pres. 2 sg., epic (= Attic ἐσθίεις): ’you devour’
ἔησθα: εἰμί — be; impf. 2 sg., epic ἔησθα (= Attic ἦσθα): ’you were’
ἔμελέν: μέλω — be a care to, concern; impf. 3 sg., accented before an enclitic: ’it was a care’
ἕρμαιος: Ἕρμαιος — of Hermes, sacred to Hermes; masc. nom. sg. adj.
ἕσσε: ἕννυμι — clothe, put clothes on; aor. 3 sg., epic -σσ-: ’clothed, put on’
ἡγεῖτο: ἡγέομαι — lead, go first (+ dat.); impf. 3 sg. mid.: ’led’
ἤκαχε: ἀκαχίζω — distress, grieve, harass; aor. 3 sg., epic reduplicated aorist: ’grieved’
ἤρτυεν: ἀρτύω — prepare, contrive; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’was preparing’
ἱεμένους: ἵεμαι (mid. of ἵημι) — hasten, be eager; pres. part. masc. acc. pl.: ’eager’
ὀπτὸν: ὀπτός — roasted, cooked; neut. acc. sg., agreeing with κρέας (grave, mid-clause form)
ὁμήλικας: ὁμήλιξ — of the same age, a peer; masc. acc. pl.: ’age-mates’
ὁσίη: ὁσίη — what is right and hallowed, sanctioned by divine law; fem. nom. sg., with ἐστί understood: ’it is holy, it is right’
ὑπερώϊα: ὑπερῷον — upper room, upper storey; neut. pl., epic ὑπερώϊα (= Attic ὑπερῷα), acc. of goal
ὠΐσθην: οἴομαι — think, suppose; aor. 1 sg. (passive form, deponent), epic ὠΐσθην (= Attic ᾠήθην): ’I thought’
ὠκύς: ὠκύς — swift, quick; masc. nom. sg.
ὡμήρησε: ὁμηρέω — meet, fall in with, join (+ dat.); aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’met’
ὡπλίζοντο: ὁπλίζω — make ready, prepare; impf. 3 pl. mid.: ’they prepared’
ῥάπτειν: ῥάπτω — stitch together, contrive; pres. inf.: ’to contrive’
ῥάπτεις: ῥάπτω — stitch together, contrive; pres. 2 sg.: ’you contrive’

__broaden__.δαιτὸς: δαίς — feast, meal; gen. sg., after κορέννυμι: ’sated with the feast’ · also gen. after δεύομαι ’lack’: ’lacking the feast’ (δαιτὸς ἐΐσης)
__broaden__.εἰρύαται: ἐρύω — draw, haul; perf. mid./pass. 3 pl., epic -αται (for -νται): ’are drawn up’ (of ships) · also ἐρύομαι (εἰρύομαι) ’guard, watch for’; perf. mid. 3 pl. with pres. sense, epic -αται (for -νται): ’are lying in wait for’
__broaden__.θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle · also with the relative ὅθι, no connective force: ὅθι θ’ ’where’
__broaden__.κ: κε(ν) (elided κ’) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὃς δέ κ’ … ἵκηται ’whoever comes’) · also + opt., potential: ’would’ (καί κ’ ἐλθὼν … εἴποιμι ’and I would go and tell’) · also + aor. indic., unreal past: ’would have’ (καί νύ κ’ … ἔδυ ’and … would have set’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause: ’will’ (τοὺς δέ κ’ … θέλξει ’and then … will enchant them’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ μέν κ’ αἰνήσωσι ’if they approve’)
__broaden__.κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν) · also + secondary indic. (κατέφθιτο), unreal past conditional: ’would have perished’ · also + aor. indic. of a future event pictured as already accomplished, an eventual near-certainty rather than a counterfactual: ἤ κεν ... κτεῖνεν ’or he may well have killed (him) already’ · also + subj. in a relative clause, prospective: ’who is to, who will’ (ἥ κεν ἄγῃσι ’(a wagon) that shall carry’) · also + opt. in a purpose clause: ’so that’ (ὥς κεν … γένοιτο ’so that he might become’) · also + subj. in a temporal clause: ’whenever’ (ὅτε κεν … δαινύῃ ’whenever you feast’) · also + subj. in the protasis of a condition after αἴ: ’if ever’ · also + opt., potential: ’might, may’ · also + opt. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἰ δέ κεν … ἀφικοίμεθα ’but if we should reach’) · also + fut. indic. or short-vowel subj. in an apodosis: ’will’ (αἶψά κεν … τεύξομεν ’at once we will build’) · also + subj. in the protasis after εἰ: ’if ever’ (εἴ κεν … ἵκωμαι ’if I should come’) · also + subj. in a disjunctive statement of what may happen: ’may’ (ἤ κεν ἁλώῃ ’or he may be caught’) · also + subj. in a general relative: ’whoever’ (ὅς κεν ὀπυίῃ ’whoever marries’) · also + subj. after εἰς ὅ, ’until’ (εἰς ὅ κεν ἔλθω ’until I come’) · also + fut. indic. in a main clause or an indirect disjunctive question: ’shall’ (ἤ κεν … δυνησόμεθ’ ’whether we shall be able’) · also + fut. indic. in a relative clause: ’who will’ (ὅς κεν … ἐποίσει ’who will lay on’)
__broaden__.μεθ: μετά (elided μεθ’ before a rough breathing) — among, with; prep. + dat. · also + acc., ’after, behind’ (μεθ’ ἡμιόνους ’behind the mules’) · also + acc., ’among’ (μεθ’ ὁμήλικας ’among his peers’)
__broaden__.μετὰ: μετά — among, with, after; prep. + dat./acc./gen. · with acc. also ’in quest of, in search of’ (μετὰ χαλκόν ’after bronze’) · also a plain adverb, no case governed: ’besides, in addition’ · also adverb, ’among them, in their midst’: μετὰ δὲ πρέπει ἀγρομένοισιν ’and he stands out among the gathered’ · also as preverb in tmesis (μετὰ … βεβήκει = μεταβεβήκει ’had moved on, passed on’) · also a plain adverb, ’afterwards’ (μετὰ γάρ τε καὶ ἄλγεσι τέρπεται ἀνήρ ’for afterwards a man takes pleasure even in pains’; some take it as ’among’ with ἄλγεσι) · also + dat. of the mind, ’in’ (μετὰ φρεσὶ σῇσι ’in your mind’)
__broaden__.πόνου: πόνος — toil, labour, hardship; masc. gen. sg., after ἄνευθε · also gen. after παύομαι ’cease from’: ’from toil’
__broaden__.σφέας: σφεῖς — they; pron., masc. acc. pl., epic σφέας (= Attic σφᾶς), governed by διά: ’through them’ · also acc. pl. object of a verb of teaching: ’them’ (σφέας … ἐδίδαξε ’taught them’) · also acc. pl. reflexive object, with αὐτούς: ’themselves’ (πυκάζοιεν σφέας αὐτούς) · also acc. pl. direct object: ’them’ (Ζεὺς σφέας τίσαιτο ’may Zeus punish them’) · also acc. pl. object of a compound verb of coming: ’them’ (σφέας εἰσαφίκηται ’comes to them’) · also acc. pl. subject of an infinitive: ’them (to be)’ (σφέας … ἔμμεναι)
__broaden__.τούς: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. pl. ’them’ · also with a noun, article-like: ’the, those’ (τούς τ’ ἄλλους ’and the others’)
__broaden__.ἐΐσης: ἐΐσος — equal, balanced, well-proportioned (of a ship; sense debated); fem. gen. sg., epic (= Attic ἴσος) · also fem. gen. sg. agreeing with δαιτός: ’equal, fair-shared’ (δαιτὸς ἐΐσης)
__broaden__.ἔλθοι: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. opt. 3 sg. (wish): ’may... come’ · also in a conditional protasis: ’if ... should come’ (εἰ καί ποθεν ἄλλοθεν ἔλθοι) · also in an indirect question after a past verb: ’from where she came’ (πόθεν ἔλθοι) · also in a relative clause with κε, prospective: ’(whoever) should come’ (ὅς κε … ἔλθοι) · also in a negative purpose clause after μή: ’lest he go’ (μή … ἔλθοι ἀπαγγέλλων)
